item.content:
Shout out to my brother Joa for encouraging me to start a blog. I’ve read and enjoyed various blogs over the years, but I hadn’t previously thought of starting one myself. I think that’s because most of the blogs I’ve read have been sort of academic or polemical or trying to sell something or otherwise created with a particular motive in mind. That’s not what this site’s about, at least not right now.

The specific idea from my brother’s blog that lodged in my head and made the whole thing sound appealing is the same one that I now posit to you, dear reader: A blog is just social media, when you think about it. Which means you don’t need a domain of expertise wherein you’re the world’s leading authority, or a radical new theory the world must know about, or anything like that. All you need is something to say, and then to sit down and type it out. It’s conceptually not too different from the ‘gram or Facebook or whatever.

Well, it it a slower medium. After I type this out, I’m going to proofread it, revise it, and perform the multi-step process of actually publishing it to the Web. More on that later. The point is, this medium demands only a little more effort than just thumbing out a Xeet and smashing Post. And since you’re already here, odds are I don’t need to sell you on the pleasures of reading or even writing longer-form content. Or if you don’t want to blog right this minute, that’s fine too. Maybe it would help if I told you a little about

What I’m Actually Doing Here

So I told you I liked the idea of writing a blog. Which is enough of a reason to sit down at the keyboard, but a sentiment is not a reason or a goal. It’s all good though. I think we all to some extent decide we like something (or don’t) and reason out the whys later. A few years ago, I had a conversation with one of my other brothers (Dominic) which was revelatory to me. About phones. He told me that he’d recently bought a new iPhone and that the first thing he did after setting it up was, he looked up reviews of that exact phone, to convince himself that it was a good phone. I became acutely aware that I had done the same thing with other consumer goods, and also with certain of my experiences, opinions, and so on. This is fine! So long as you do your epistemic due dilligence of course. So now I’m going to kind of do two things simultaneously. I’m going to reason backward, from sentiment to text, and I’m also going to expound on the point of this paragraph.

Creating a neural prosthetic

item.title: About
item.author: Isaac Kennedy
item.content:
Me

Hi there!

I’m a technical writer currently based in South Bend, Indiana. I’m originally from Nashville. In my free time, I play tennis and pickleball, explore new parts of the region, and tend to my aquariums. I’m currently taking a B2-level course in Spanish. That’s pretty much what I’m up to these days. I have various other interests as well, but I’ll leave it at that for now.

This site

is protean (at least for now), subject to change at my whim. Think of it as my social media page. Except I own the place and so there’s no algorithm Skinner box slop, ads, et cetera. Whether you’re a family member or friend or just someone who Googled me for whatever reason, this is where you can see what I’ve been doing, my takes, where my head’s at in a general sense.

Stick around and you might see reviews, treatises, rants, or even an occasional windshield musing that was good enough to type out and post. There may be frequent changes to the content, theme, or overall look of the site. Expect a slight roughness around the edges while I get this thing dialed in.
